content.overview: BNS s. 315 — Dishonest misappropriation of property possessed by deceased person at the time of his death.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Dishonest misappropriation of property possessed by deceased person at the time of his death. BNS restatement of IPC 404. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 404. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 315 is the rule on “Dishonest misappropriation of property possessed by deceased person at the time of his death”. The section provides that whoever dishonestly misappropriates or converts to his own use any property, knowing that such property was in the possession of a deceased person at the time of that person’s decease, and has not since been in the possession of any person legally entitled to such possession, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine, and if the offender at the time of such person’s decease was employed by him as a clerk or servant, the imprisonment may extend to seven years. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 315 exists so that “Dishonest misappropriation of property possessed by deceased person at the time of his death” has a closed legal test in Chapter XVII — Of Offences Against Property. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Theft, snatching, extortion, robbery, dacoity, trust, cheating, mischief, trespass.

The provision in detail
315. Whoever dishonestly misappropriates or converts to his own use any property, knowing that such property was in the possession of a deceased person at the time of that person’s decease, and has not since been in the possession of any person legally entitled to such possession, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine, and if the offender at the time of such person’s decease was employed by him as a clerk or servant, the imprisonment may extend to seven years

Essential ingredients
1. Whoever dishonestly misappropriates or converts to his own use any property, knowing that such property was in the possession of a deceased person at the time of that person’s decease, and has not since been in the possession of any person legally entitled to such possession, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine, and if the offender at the time of such person’s decease was employed by him as a clerk or servant, the imprisonment may extend to seven years

Statutory illustrations
Illustration (a). Z dies in possession of furniture and money. His servant A, before the money comes into the possession of any person entitled to such possession, dishonestly misappropriates it. A has committed the offence defined in this section

Exam use: quote illustration (a), then write which ingredient of BNS s. 315 it proves. Copying the illustration without that mapping sentence does not score.
